text.t: Hemoglobin is four protein chains packed together: two alpha chains and two beta chains.
This is the protein that makes blood red and carries oxygen around your body.
Chains A and C are the alpha chains, each 141 amino acids long in this file.
Each chain holds a flat, ring-shaped heme group with one iron atom at its centre.
Oxygen binds to that iron, so one hemoglobin can carry four oxygen molecules.

tour.title: The histidine that holds the iron

text.t: Histidine 87 reaches up from below the heme and bonds to the iron.
When oxygen lands on the iron it pulls this histidine, and the shift spreads to the other chains so they grab oxygen more easily.
Position 6 of each beta chain is glutamate in normal hemoglobin.
In sickle cell hemoglobin it is valine, and that one change lets the molecules stick together into stiff fibers.
This structure is deoxyhemoglobin, the form with no oxygen bound.

does.t: Hemoglobin picks up oxygen in the lungs and carries it through the blood to the rest of the body.
Each molecule binds up to four oxygen molecules, one at each iron.
It also carries some carbon dioxide away from the tissues.

shape.t: The four chains work as a team: the first oxygen is hard to add, then the second, third and fourth bind more and more easily.
When oxygen binds to one iron, it pulls a histidine and shifts a helix, and that motion rocks the neighbouring chains into a shape that grabs oxygen faster.
The same teamwork works in reverse in the tissues, so once one oxygen drops off the rest are released quickly.

text.t: Hemoglobin lives inside red blood cells, about 250 million molecules in each cell.
Mammal red blood cells have no organelles, which leaves more room for hemoglobin.

wrong.t: In sickle cell disease, glutamate 6 of the beta chain is replaced by valine.
Without oxygen these hemoglobins stick together into long fibers that bend red blood cells into a sickle shape and can clog blood vessels.
Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it takes oxygen's place on the heme and is hard to remove.

history.who: G. Fermi, M.F. Perutz, B. Shaanan and R. Fourme

text.t: This human deoxyhemoglobin structure was refined at 1.74 angstroms using X-rays from a synchrotron.
Max Perutz had earlier solved the groundbreaking structure of horse hemoglobin, which is also in the Protein Data Bank.

compare.t: From its farthest atom to its farthest atom, this hemoglobin measures about 7 nm.
About 250 million of them fit inside a single red blood cell.

text.t: Glutamate 6 of the beta chain becomes valine in sickle cell hemoglobin.
This histidine bonds to the heme iron from below.
In the beta chains the histidine that bonds to the iron is number 92.
